config.title: Event Typing

intro.title: Event Typing
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that responds to different keyboard events. You will learn how to type event handlers to ensure they correctly receive and process specific event objects, like KeyboardEvent. The core concept is using TypeScript or Vue's built-in type inference to define the expected event structure, improving code safety and developer experience. You will work with Vue's template syntax, event listeners, and type annotations. By the end, you'll understand how to handle events in a type-safe way within a Vue application.
intro.usecase: Event typing is essential in Vue applications where user interactions drive dynamic behavior, such as form validation in sign-up flows where each keystroke triggers immediate feedback. In interactive dashboards, typing events control real-time data filtering and search functionality across tables and charts. Developers use typed events to build responsive components like autocomplete inputs, live character counters, and keyboard-navigable menus, ensuring type safety and preventing runtime errors in production applications.

objectives: Apply TypeScript type annotations to Vue event handlers
Construct typed event handler functions for common DOM events
Implement type-safe event binding in Vue template syntax
Configure component methods to receive properly typed event parameters
Manipulate event objects while maintaining type safety
Initialize event handlers with explicit parameter types
Integrate native Event types with Vue's event system

steps.title: Import Vue and ref
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from 'vue' to use reactive state in your component.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a package
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref function are imported, ready for use in the component.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported something, but make sure to import both Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement. You need to import both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named EventTypingDemo using the <script setup> syntax and a template with a root <div> element.
steps.hint: Use the <script setup> tag to define the component. The template should have a single root element, typically a <div>.
steps.analogousExample: // Example of a basic Vue component with script setup
steps.expectedOutcome: The component structure is set up with a script setup block and a template containing a root <div> element.
successCriteria: The component is named EventTypingDemo (implicitly by filename or usage), uses <script setup>, and has a template with a root <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the <script setup> block and a template with a single root element (like <div>).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Remember to use <script setup> for the logic and <template> with a root element for the structure.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state for input value
steps.instruction: Inside the <script setup> section, use ref to create a reactive state variable called 'inputValue' with an initial value of an empty string.
steps.hint: You can create a reactive reference using the ref function imported earlier. Declare it as a constant.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating reactive state for a counter
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a reactive state variable 'inputValue' that will store user input from events.
successCriteria: A reactive variable 'inputValue' is declared using ref with an initial value of empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref to create a reactive variable called 'inputValue' with an empty string as the initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a reactive state variable using the ref function.

steps.title: Define a handler for input events
steps.instruction: Inside the <script setup> section, define a function named handleInput that takes an event parameter and updates the inputValue state with the event's target value.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives an event object and sets inputValue.value to event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named handleInput is defined that updates inputValue when called with an input event.
successCriteria: The handleInput function is defined, takes an event parameter, and sets inputValue.value to event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it updates inputValue.value with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Check that it takes an event parameter and updates the inputValue state.

steps.title: Add an input element to the template
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add an <input> element with type='text' to capture user input.
steps.hint: Place the <input> element inside the <div> in your template. Use the type attribute to specify it as a text input.
steps.analogousExample: // Adding an input element to a template
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains an <input> element that will allow users to type text.
successCriteria: An <input> element with type='text' is present inside the template's <div>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added an <input> element with type='text' inside the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing or incorrect. Add an <input> element with type='text' to the template.

steps.title: Bind the input value to reactive state
steps.instruction: In the template, add the v-model directive to the input element to bind it to the inputValue reactive state variable.
steps.hint: Use v-model to create two-way data binding between the input and the reactive state.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Similar: binding an input to reactive state -->
<input v-model="username" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element will be bound to the inputValue reactive state using v-model.
successCriteria: The input element has the v-model directive set to "inputValue".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added v-model to the input element with the correct state variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is not properly bound to the reactive state. Check that you've used v-model correctly.

steps.title: Add an event listener for input changes
steps.instruction: Add an @input event listener to the input element that calls your handler function.
steps.hint: Use the @input directive to attach an event listener that triggers your handler when the input value changes.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding an event listener to an input
<input @input="handleInput" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element will have an @input event listener that calls your handler function.
successCriteria: The input element includes an @input attribute that references the handler function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the @input attribute to the input element.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the @input event listener to the input element.

steps.title: Display the current input value
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element below the input to display the current input value using Vue's template interpolation.
steps.hint:
Use the

tag and display the value of inputValue inside it with double curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying reactive state in a paragraph

{{ message }}
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element showing the current input value appears below the input field.
successCriteria: A paragraph element with {{ inputValue }} is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the value of inputValue using double curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element is missing or doesn't display the input value correctly.

steps.title: Add a button to clear the input
steps.instruction: Add a button element after the input with a click handler that clears the inputValue state.
steps.hint: Use the <button> tag with @click directive to call a function that sets inputValue to an empty string.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="clearInput">Clear</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears after the input that, when clicked, will clear the input field.
successCriteria: Button element is added with @click event handler that sets inputValue to empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has an @click handler that sets inputValue to ''.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or doesn't have the correct click handler to clear the input value.

steps.title: Define the clear input handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named clearInput that sets inputValue to an empty string.
steps.hint: Create a function that updates the reactive state variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: A clearInput function is defined that resets the input value.
successCriteria: The clearInput function is defined and sets inputValue to ''.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named clearInput and sets inputValue to an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The clearInput function is not properly defined. Check the function name and that it sets inputValue to ''.
